Interest rates likely to rise tomorrow, but is a second sting coming before Christmas?
The Reserve Bank is meeting tomorrow for the sixth time this year, and both financial markets and economists think it is almost certain that it will raise interest rates for the fourth time.
Another standard 25-basis-point rate hike tomorrow would take the RBA's cash rate target from 4.35 per cent to 4.6 per cent, the highest level since the start of November 2011.
So, how does the bank make its decision, what does it mean for your mortgage and how much higher do experts think interest rates might go?

Finance minister flags Labor will introduce AI reforms before end of year
Katy Gallagher is out in the press gallery corridors to spruik that $6 billion improvement to the budget deficit and she's been asked about artificial intelligence.
Labor has flagged introducing legislation to impose "guardrails" on artificial intelligence following the OpenAI agent hack.
The finance minister says the government would be keen to introduce its planned AI reforms to parliament before the end of the year.

"This is a new area of reform so a bit of work to do there. Hopefully the OpenAI incident of the last week that we reported will be considered by this joint select committee gives people a really clear example of why we need some legislative guardrails here," Gallagher says.

"I think there's a lot of goodwill across the parliament to try and see what's possible. Certainly the opposition are talking by the end of this year and I think if that's possible that would be ideal."
Paterson says penalties for AI hacks should be reserved for most serious cases
Shadow Defence Minister James Paterson says discussion about penalties for OpenAI over the rogue agent hack is "too silly for words".
A rogue agent breached the Services Australia portal without instruction from the company on June 18.
Paterson had told ABC Radio National Breakfast the question of liability needs to be resolved, but that it relied on determining intent.
He says an AI agent that is misaligned with its human master doesn't necessarily reflect the intent of the person who programmed it.
The shadow minister says penalties must be reserved for the most serious cases.
"This is a thorny and important policy issue to resolve. But I have to say, some of the conversation about criminal penalties about the most recent incident are too silly for words," Paterson says.

"If a teenager replicated this exact data access, there's no way that we would charge them with anything and they could do it happily from their mum and dad's basement on a basic laptop without an AI agent."
Pressure on government budget is increasing, Gallagher says
Katy Gallagher says pressures on the government's budget is increasing in areas such as aged care, health and defence spending.
The treasurer is set to announce a $6 billion improvement to the budget deficit, lower than the $28.3 billion deficit forecast in the budget in May.
Speaking to ABC Radio National Breakfast, Gallagher says the war in the Middle East is also placing pressure on the budget.
"The decisions we have to take are what are the right and sensible decisions to be making about investments, but how do we also find savings and get the budget in better shape," Gallagher says.
Key Event
Gallagher says OpenAI should face consequences for agent hack
Finance Minister Katy Gallagher says OpenAI should face consequences for the rogue agent breach on a government portal.
The agent hacked a Services Australia statistics portal on June 18, but the government wasn't informed of the breach until September 10.
Gallagher has told ABC Radio National Breakfast that while the breach presented as "unusual activity" in Services Australia's system, it wasn't enough to raise a red flag.
The finance minister says while the company should face consequences, she's stopped short of saying they should be prosecuted.
She says a mandatory reporting requirement for tech companies that discover their systems have breached a government site should be a minimum.

"I think there should be consequences, but I also have been briefed very clearly that OpenAI have been helping us and helping us not just in relation to kind of making sure that vulnerable issue has been dealt with," Gallagher says.

"I think we have to have a look at this incident and deal with it on its merits. But the broader question of how we deal with these in the future, we've got to be looking at legislation, but also engagement with these companies."
Key Event
Gallagher says email used to report cyber vulnerabilities moved to 24/7 centre
Katy Gallagher says an email used by OpenAI to report an agent hack has been moved to a 24/7 centre that monitors cybersecurity.
OpenAI first sent an email to Services Australia about the hack on September 10, but the department didn't see the email until the next day.
The finance minister says the email has been moved to a centre within the department that monitors cybersecurity risks around the clock.
She has told ABC News Breakfast the artificial intelligence company has provided the government with all the information it has asked for.

"That is a good thing because we need to verify what they are telling us. They are sharing their technical data, their logs, and that is helping us absolutely provide that assurance to the public that their information is safe," Gallagher says.
Gina Rinehart allegedly tried to help recruit Liberal MP Henry Pike to join One Nation
One Nation's billionaire backer Gina Rinehart allegedly attempted to help recruit a sitting federal Liberal MP after he was invited for lunch at one of her holiday homes.
Henry Pike represents the seat of Bowman for Queensland's Liberal National Party and has previously held fundraisers hosted by Rinehart.

In January, he arrived at the mining magnate's $34 million Sunshine Coast beach house to find One Nation leader Pauline Hanson, her then chief-of-staff James Ashby and federal MP Barnaby Joyce were staying there.
Coalition sources have told Four Corners that during the lunch, Rinehart asked Pike if he was thinking of joining One Nation or would ever consider it.
Read the full story from Steve Cannane, Alex McDonald and Lara Sonnenschein from Four Corners in the link below.
Plibersek defends cost-of-living assistance ahead of interest rate decision
Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek has defended Labor's cost-of-living assistance ahead of an expected interest rate hike tomorrow.
The Reserve Bank will announce its interest rate decision, with the continuing Middle East war expected to factor in the decision.
Speaking to Channel Seven with One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce, Plibersek has spruiked Labor's efforts to increase bulk billing and lower prescription costs.
"The fundamentals of the Australian economy are very strong and what we want to do is take those day-to-day pressures off Australians. We're doing that," Plibersek says.
Asked how Joyce would make people's lives better, the One Nation MP said he would stop spending money on renewable energy.
"Our inflation rate is the highest of the developed countries. Let's just get that correct. The highest in developed countries. And that's making people poorer," Joyce says.
But pressed on what policies One Nation brings, Joyce has raised the idea of refurbishing every coal-fired power station.

"Well, you can't do much better than Snowy Hydro 2.0. I'll say Malcolm Turnbull's baby is going to cost $2 billion, now it's $42 billion. You could have refurbished every power station in Australia with that money that."
Key Event
Treasurer set to unveil $6 billion boost to federal budget
Treasurer Jim Chalmers and Finance Minister Katy Gallagher are today set to unveil a $6 billion improvement to the federal budget.
The Final Budget Outcome for 2025-26 is expected to show a deficit $6 billion lower than the $28.3 billion deficit forecast in the budget in May.
The announcement comes just a day before the Reserve Bank of Australia looks set to increase interest rates for the fourth time this year.
Labor has consistently pointed to gross debt as a percentage of GDP being lower than other major advanced economies such as the US, Canada and the UK.
